title: Policy, value, and entropy in one objective
goal:
When the policy and value function share parameters, Section 5 combines three terms into one objective (Equation 9):

$$L_t^{CLIP+VF+S}(\theta) = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t\big[L_t^{CLIP}(\theta) - c_1 L_t^{VF}(\theta) + c_2 S[\pi_\theta](s_t)\big]$$

where $L_t^{VF} = (V_\theta(s_t) - V_t^{targ})^2$ and $S$ is the entropy of the policy.

The inputs are `probs` and `probs_old`, arrays of shape `(N, K)` with one action distribution per row, `actions` (integer array of length $N$), `adv`, `values` ($V_\theta(s_t)$), and `returns` ($V_t^{targ}$). The starter gives you the finished `clip_term`. Write:

- `entropy(probs)` returns the entropy in nats of each row, an array of length $N$.
- `ppo_objective(probs, probs_old, actions, adv, values, returns, eps, c1, c2)` returns the scalar of Equation 9. The paper maximizes it.
- `ppo_loss(...)` takes the same arguments and returns the value to minimize.
hints: Entropy is $-\sum_k p_k \log p_k$ over the last axis. For a uniform distribution over $K$ actions it is $\log K$.
The ratio is $\pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t) / \pi_{\theta_{old}}(a_t \mid s_t)$. Pick the chosen action out of each row with `probs[np.arange(N), actions]`.

The value loss is squared, and it has a minus sign in the objective, because you maximize the objective and want the value error to shrink. The entropy has a plus sign, because you want a high entropy.
A loss that you minimize is the negative of the objective.
